note: Creature behaviour as data (roadmap item 48; core/game/game_behaviour.gd, checked by tools/check_data.gd). A creature in the open world needs no code of its own: it has TAGS, each tag sets some of the parameters below (the global `order` decides which tag wins when two set the same one, so the order a creature lists its tags in does not matter), and `GameBehaviour.step` is one small state machine that reads the parameters. Modes: idle and wander (a random walk on keyed dice, held to `wander_radius` of home), chase (hostile and it sees a target; `leash` or a guard's `guard_radius` ends it and it returns home), flee (hurt below `flee_hp`, or skittish and something is close, until it is `flee_dist` away), herd (kept within `herd_radius` of its kind's centre), ambush (still until a target is within `ambush_range`, then a burst), and the pack: `swarm` creatures in creatures.json are a pack, one that sees a target alerts its kind within `alert_radius`, and the pack spreads round the target instead of queueing: each member takes its own bearing to either side of the pack's approach (`flank_spread`, in radians) and circles in at it, closing on the target itself within `flank` tiles; `flank_close` is how fast the circle shrinks. Ground creatures are held off ground the caller says they cannot walk on; fliers are not. Night is a flag the caller gives (the world has no clock of the day yet, item 51). Every die is keyed on the seed, the creature and the tick, never the dynasty's.

predator.about: Hunts: sees far, follows far, and runs faster than it walks.

ambusher.about: Lies still until something comes within a few tiles, then bursts out.

nocturnal.about: Sees far at night and is half asleep by day.

territorial.about: Keeps to its own ground: gives up the chase when drawn far from home.

guardian.about: Holds a post: stands near it and only fights what comes within its reach.

berserk.about: Never flees, and fights harder when hurt.

flier.about: Goes where it likes, over water and rock.

docile.about: Does not attack, and keeps to a small patch.

skittish.about: Runs from anything that comes close.

herd.about: Keeps together with its own kind.
